author_or_org: METR (Joel Becker, Nate Rush, Tom Cunningham, David Rein, Khalid Mahamud)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: METR's earlier paper found that AI tools caused a 20% slowdown in completing tasks among experienced open-source developers, using data from February to June 2025.
claims.quote: which found the use of AI tools caused a 20% slowdown in completing tasks among experienced open-source developers, using data from February to June 2025.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: METR's early 2025 study found AI use caused tasks to take 19% longer, with a confidence interval from +2% to +39%.
claims.quote: Our early 2025 study found the use of AI causes tasks to take 19% longer, with a confidence interval between +2% and +39%.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: For the subset of original developers in the later study, METR estimated a speedup of -18%, with a confidence interval from -38% to +9%.
claims.quote: For the subset of the original developers who participated in the later study, we now estimate a speedup of -18% with a confidence interval between -38% and +9%.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Among newly recruited developers, METR estimated a speedup of -4%, with a confidence interval from -15% to +9%.
claims.quote: Among newly-recruited developers the estimated speedup is -4%, with a confidence interval between -15% and +9%.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: METR observed more developers declining to participate because they did not want to work without AI, which likely biases the AI-assisted speedup estimate downward.
claims.quote: The primary reason is that we have observed a significant increase in developers choosing not to participate in the study because they do not wish to work without AI, which likely biases downwards our estimate of AI-assisted speedup.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: When surveyed, 30% to 50% of developers reported withholding some tasks because they did not want to do them without AI.
claims.quote: When surveyed, 30% to 50% of developers told us that they were choosing not to submit some tasks because they did not want to do them without AI.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Some developers reported that final work quality differed between AI-allowed and AI-disallowed conditions, including subjective code quality and the amount of documentation or tests created.
claims.quote: Some developers told us the quality of the final work, for a given task, was different between AI-allowed and AI-disallowed conditions, e.g. differences in subjective code quality, or the amount of documentation or tests they chose to create.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Developers sometimes self-report very high speedups, but METR says those estimates can be quite unreliable.
claims.quote: Some developers self-report very high speedups, though as we documented in our earlier study those estimates can be quite unreliable.
